# Vector Law

**What this is:** the law firm that runs the abandoned-home auction when a lien exists on the home — the lien-present counterpart to Florida Fast Title in the eviction process.

**Status:** current — 2026-08-30

## The facts
- **What they supply:** the auction of a repossessed manufactured home **where a lien is present**. Vector Law posts the auction and communicates the auction date back to Parakeet (SOP 107, step 34b).
- **Who uses it:** the **Evictions Team**, at the point in SOP 107 after the Writ of Possession has issued and the Community Manager has reported the home's identifying detail (VIN / HUD number / decal / tag number, make, model, year, length, width). The split is explicit: **no lien → Florida Fast Title; lien exists → Vector Law.**
- Everything upstream is identical either way — the demand notice cadence, the attorney intake packet, the court process, the writ, the post-writ inspection. Vector Law only picks up at the auction fork.
- **How critical: high.** Every liened home that comes back through eviction has exactly one documented route out, and it is Vector Law. Without them a liened repossession has nowhere to go: the home sits on a lot, unsellable and unrentable, with the lien unresolved. There is no second lien-auction vendor named anywhere in 242 process files.
- **The volume it protects:** SOP 107 is a Tier 1 Critical monthly cycle across the whole portfolio, and the RV variant on the intake form ("Is home worth more than $500.00?") shows how low the value floor goes — so this path handles the assets least worth spending money on and most expensive to leave in place.
- **Known problems — the lien path is documented in one sentence and nowhere else.** Vector Law appears in SOP 107's auction step and in the library's systems list, and that is all. **Neither the post-eviction title SOP nor the resident turn-in SOP mentions Vector Law or liens at all**, so once the auction is with Vector Law there is no documented process for the title work that follows it — no package contents, no clock, no escalation, no owner.
- No SOP states who determines whether a lien exists, how it is searched, or what evidence is filed — only that the answer routes the home to one vendor or the other.
- Vector Law is separate from the eviction attorney in SOP 107, who receives the monthly intake packets in the last week of the month and must confirm in writing before an eviction workflow can be closed. Nothing in the library says whether they are the same firm.
- The related counsel gap is the wider one: the 14 state compliance SOPs all sit at counsel review with no sign-off, and **Massachusetts and North Carolina have no compliance SOPs at all** — so there is no state-specific lien or abandonment guidance behind this vendor outside Florida.
